title: Kernel auto-selection v2: core decision logic + selector interfaces
author: Yuki Sato
description:
Implements the *core* kernel auto-selection v2 decision engine (feature extraction + candidate generation + scoring/decision rules) and formalizes the selector interfaces used by the runtime execution path.

This PR is intentionally scoped to the selector’s internal API and baseline behavior. Rollout gates, model-family classifier improvements, seq-length regime bucketing, GPU SKU registry + denylist, and telemetry are handled in follow-up PRs (see linked work).

Motivation
- v1 selection is primarily model-agnostic and tends to overfit to “average” prompt lengths.
- We need predictable selection behavior that can incorporate signals like (model family, seq-length regime, GPU SKU) while remaining deterministic + explainable.

What’s included
- New module: `KernelSelectorV2`
  - Deterministic decision function: (request features + environment features + registry) -> selection result
  - Candidate generation API that returns ordered candidates with reasons
  - Explicit fallback hierarchy (safe default kernel + “known stable” fallback)
- Feature extraction (v2 baseline)
  - Model identifier normalization hooks (no classifier changes in this PR; consumes `ModelInfo` fields already available)
  - Request shape features: prefill tokens, max_new_tokens, is_streaming, batch_size_hint
  - Runtime env features: gpu_arch (coarse), compute_capability, cuda_version (coarse)
  - Seq regime is a stubbed enum in this PR (wired but populated by follow-up bucketing work)
- Decision rules (v2 baseline)
  - Rule ordering is explicit and stable (no map iteration / unordered set iteration in decision path)
  - Scoring is rule-based (ADR-017 direction) with a deterministic tie-break
  - Hard guardrails:
    - If registry has no compatible kernels -> return `Fallback(Default)`
    - If candidate is marked “experimental” and request is long-context -> deprioritize
- Baseline tests
  - Unit tests for stable ordering and tie-break behavior
  - Replay test scaffold (feeds fixed input vectors and asserts exact selection) (full deterministic replay suite in later PR)
  - Snapshot tests for selection explanation strings (to keep reasoning stable for oncall debugging)

Not included / follow-ups
- GPU SKU keying and denylist support (PR #28452)
- Seq-length bucketing + prefill/decode heuristics (PR #28439)
- Model-family classifier + rule specializations (PR #28428)
- Feature gate + config plumbing (PR #28460)
- Telemetry emission + sampling policy (PR #28466)

Docs/refs
- Design: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-auto-selection-v2-design
- ADR: confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-017-kernel-auto-selection-v2-features-and-fallbacks

Risk
- This PR adds a new codepath but it is not enabled by default; callsites are wired such that v1 remains authoritative until the feature gate lands.
- The selector is deterministic by construction (no randomness, no time-based decisions, no unordered iteration).

Testing
- `bazel test //runtime/kernels/selector:all`
- `bazel test //runtime/executor:selector_integration_test`
- Lightweight perf smoke: selector evaluation overhead microbench stub (full microbench in benchmark-lab PR #811)

Checklist
- [x] Deterministic ordering for candidates
- [x] No new allocations in hot path beyond candidate vector (bounded)
- [x] Clear fallback behavior + reason strings
- [x] Baseline unit tests + replay scaffolding
- [ ] Telemetry fields (follow-up)
- [ ] Feature gate (follow-up)

Notes on INT-10411
- This PR adds structured “reason strings” and stable keys for selection outcomes, to reduce metric cardinality surprises when we begin emitting telemetry (telemetry PR will reference these stable keys).

review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Candidate ordering looks good, but can you guarantee no unordered_map iteration leaks into score tie-breaks? We’ve been burned by that before on kernel registries.

Yuki Sato (author): Yep. I removed iteration over registry maps in the final selection pass. Candidate vector is built in a stable order by explicit registry priority list + stable kernel_id sort. Added test `TieBreak_StableAcrossInsertionOrder` to cover this.
Noah Patel: Please add an explicit comment about determinism invariants and the allowed inputs (no time/random). Also want the fallback precedence to be enumerated, not implied by score constants.
Yuki Sato (author): Added `DeterminismContract` docstring in selector_v2.h and refactored fallback to an explicit enum precedence list. Also expanded unit tests to assert fallback reason keys.
Omar El-Sayed: Reason strings are helpful, but please ensure the keys are stable and low-cardinality. We should not emit full model names or request ids in the explanation.

Yuki Sato (author): Agreed. Explanations are split into (stable reason_key + human-readable detail). Tests assert reason_key set. No request IDs, and model name is only used in debug logs (not in reason detail).
Sofia Ivanova: The request features include `batch_size_hint` — where is that sourced and is it safe for scheduler-driven mixed workloads?
Yuki Sato (author): For now it’s optional and defaults to 1. The scheduler-derived hints will be plumbed in later (PR #28502). This PR only defines the interface + uses provided value if present.
Anika Gupta: Can we add a negative test that fails if the candidate list changes when registry insertion order changes?
Yuki Sato (author): Added `CandidateList_StableAcrossRegistryPermutation` and made registry test helper generate random insertion orders under a fixed seed; asserts identical results.
final_merge_note: Merged via squash after addressing determinism comments and adding stable reason_key tests. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4821 and linked PRs for gating/telemetry/SKU+seq features.
